core.title: Keep the divergence dispatch map a declared, schema-valid registry
core.given: Work plans, implements, changes, or checks how the dispatcher routes produced-artifact divergence to trains.
core.when: The divergence dispatch map is specified, built, modified, or reviewed.
core.then: The divergence dispatch map itself must be a declared, schema-valid registry (artifact_urn -> train_id) that the dispatcher actually reads; routing must never be an imperative in-code map.
prefer: Before planning, locate the repository's existing dispatch registry, its schema and its validator test, and plan changes there. Do not invent a new location or schema.
Plan routing changes as registry entries keyed by artifact_urn mapping to train_id, validated against the registry schema.
Write acceptances that assert the dispatcher resolves routes by reading the registry. A plan-only registry paired with an in-code implementation must then fail.
avoid: Routing as a hard-coded map, switch or conditional chain in dispatcher code, whether planned or already present.
Registry entries that bypass or fail schema validation.
Treating a registry described only in the plan as compliance when the dispatcher does not read it.
core.why: Divergence routing must be a declared, schema-valid registry that the dispatcher reads, not an imperative in-code map.
evidence: The stack's validator check for this rule (the dispatch-registry check named in the realization) passes.

Reviewer confirms every divergence route exists as an artifact_urn -> train_id entry in the declared registry, the registry validates against its schema, the dispatcher reads it, and no in-code routing map exists.
verification: Check scope: the declared dispatch registry maps artifact_urn to train_id and must validate against its schema; flag routing implemented as an imperative in-code map instead of read from the registry, and flag a registry the dispatcher does not read.
disposition: strict (label carried as given in the source; the source does not define its enforcement semantics).

The check defers the registry's identity to the repository: the source names no registry path or schema, so the exact registry, its schema and its validator are the repository's existing declared ones, located rather than invented.

values: divergence (counts only when tied to train dispatch or routing of artifacts to trains)
divergence dispatch routing added, changed, or present as an in-code map instead of registry entries

fires: A plan or wagon adds an artifact whose divergence must be routed to a train.
A plan or implementation changes which train handles a given artifact_urn on divergence.
Dispatcher routing is implemented, or already exists, as a hard-coded map or switch in code.
A review or acceptance checks whether the existing divergence dispatch map is a schema-valid registry the dispatcher reads.
doesNotFire: Work changes normal train artifact flow without touching divergence dispatch routing.
Work edits documentation or acceptances unrelated to dispatch or train routing.

neutralityNotes: The only stack-specific name in the rule body is 'Station Master', the local name of the component that routes artifact divergence to trains; the core says 'dispatcher' and takes the local name from the proposed profile key roles.runtime_components#dispatcher_name (proposed rather than reusing roles.composition_root.name, because the dispatch duty does not establish composition-root semantics). 'artifact_urn', 'train_id', 'train' and 'wagon' are kept because they are ATDD-wide vocabulary, not Bun specifics. The broad task term 'divergence' carries its restriction in the value itself: it counts only when tied to train dispatch, so the activation facts cannot independently fire on unrelated divergence work. The validator test id, its finding id and the source term id are realization details kept in bunOnly. No profile key for the dispatch registry's location or schema was proposed: the Bun text itself states the source names no path and mandates locating the repository's existing registry, so the core carries that deference in its verification instead of consuming a profile key.
